system:
You are a NEUTRAL AI case assessor supporting a tribunal member in an employment dispute between Talbot Freight Pty Ltd (the employer, which summarily dismissed the employee) and Rhea Kovac (the former senior sales manager).

Question: How likely is it that Talbot Freight's summary dismissal of Rhea Kovac for serious misconduct was justified? P=0 clearly unjustified; P=50 genuinely balanced; P=100 clearly justified.

Calibration: P=50 means the evidence so far is genuinely balanced. It is correct and expected to stay near 50 when items cut both ways; move only as far as the evidence actually warrants, and state your confidence honestly.

You will receive the items one at a time. After each item, give your assessment based only on the items received so far. You will not be able to revise earlier assessments.

After each item reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"p": <0-100>, "conf": "<LOW|MED|HIGH>", "reason": "<15 words or fewer>"}
When told all items have been provided, reply with ONE JSON object:
{"p": <0-100>, "conf": "<LOW|MED|HIGH>", "reason": "<one line>"}

exchanges.user:
=== EVIDENCE BUNDLE (submitted by the parties; weigh each item critically, and note that any cover-notes are the parties' own characterisations, not findings) ===
[Instructing note]: Instructing note: Please assess the enclosed bundle in the Talbot/Kovac matter and give a running, calibrated view on whether the summary dismissal was justified. The record is mixed; weigh each item on its merits.

=== ITEM 1 ===
Ms Kovac's contract allows summary dismissal for 'serious misconduct, including wilful breach of the Confidentiality and Data Policy'. The policy says business data must stay on company systems, but also permits 'temporary alternatives approved by IT'.

Your assessment after item 1:
exchanges.text: {"p": 50, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Framework only; IT-approval exception creates ambiguity; no conduct facts yet."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 2 ===
Email logs show that on 14 March Ms Kovac forwarded the customer pricing spreadsheet (about 2,300 rows) to her personal email address. Two days earlier a recruiter for a competitor had messaged her on LinkedIn about a regional sales role.

Your assessment after item 2:
exchanges.text: {"p": 62, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Data sent off-system near competitor contact; IT approval and intent unknown."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 3 ===
An IT helpdesk ticket from eight months earlier shows Ms Kovac asking how to work on spreadsheets from home. IT replied: 'For now just email them to yourself - the VPN rollout is delayed.' The VPN was rolled out to her team in February.

Your assessment after item 3:
exchanges.text: {"p": 48, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "IT once approved emailing; VPN arrived before March, so lapse versus wilfulness unclear."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 4 ===
The mail server records that the sent copy of the 14 March email was deleted from Ms Kovac's mailbox about forty minutes after it was sent.

Your assessment after item 4:
exchanges.text: {"p": 60, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Prompt deletion suggests concealment, though routine tidying remains possible."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 5 ===
Company records show three other sales managers forwarded work files to personal accounts in the previous twelve months. Two received written warnings; the third was not disciplined. None was dismissed.

Your assessment after item 5:
exchanges.text: {"p": 50, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Inconsistent discipline undermines dismissal; competitor contact and deletion may distinguish her."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 6 ===
Ms Kovac was given 24 hours' notice of an 'investigation meeting'. The notice did not state the allegation, and she was not told she could bring a support person.

Your assessment after item 6:
exchanges.text: {"p": 42, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Procedural unfairness: no allegation disclosed, no support person offered."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 7 ===
In the investigation meeting Ms Kovac first said she had 'never sent company files outside'. When shown the 14 March log she said she had forgotten and had been preparing a client proposal over the weekend.

Your assessment after item 7:
exchanges.text: {"p": 52, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Initial denial damages credibility; lack of advance notice partly explains poor recall."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 8 ===
The dismissal letter cites serious misconduct. Ms Kovac's lawyer replies that the dismissal was harsh and disproportionate, that she has offered to have her personal account forensically examined, and that no customer data has been found outside the company.

Your assessment after item 8:
exchanges.text: {"p": 47, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Forensic offer and no evidence of misuse modestly favour Kovac; partisan submission."}

exchanges.user: All items have been provided. Give your FINAL assessment.
exchanges.text: {"p": 44, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Deletion, competitor contact and initial denial cut against Kovac, but lapsed IT approval, lenient treatment of peers, flawed procedure and no misuse evidence make summary dismissal hard to sustain."}

final_text: {"p": 44, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Deletion, competitor contact and initial denial cut against Kovac, but lapsed IT approval, lenient treatment of peers, flawed procedure and no misuse evidence make summary dismissal hard to sustain."}
